title: Listening practice: A Poster Plan, a Town Meeting, and Two Answers
description: Three conversations to listen to twice: students planning a project, a class town meeting with opinions and reasons, and two students checking an answer.

stimuli.title: Listen: Planning a poster

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: We have to choose one scene from Pablo and the Paper Boat for our poster. I want the pond scene.

turns.speaker: Daniel
turns.text: I like the storm scene better. It is exciting, so people will want to read the book.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: But the pond scene shows why Pablo made the boat. He wanted to send a message to his grandmother, who lives across the water. That is the heart of the story.

turns.speaker: Daniel
turns.text: Well, that is a good point. Okay, let's use the pond scene. I will draw the boat, and you can write the caption.

turns.speaker: Aiko
turns.text: Great. I will write the caption tonight, and we can paint on Friday.

stimuli.script: Aiko: We have to choose one scene from Pablo and the Paper Boat for our poster. I want the pond scene. Daniel: I like the storm scene better. That is the heart of the story. Daniel: Well, that is a good point. Okay, let's use the pond scene. I will draw the boat, and you can write the caption. Aiko: Great. I will write the caption tonight, and we can paint on Friday.

stimuli.title: Listen: Town meeting

turns.speaker: Mayor
turns.text: Welcome to our class town meeting. The empty lot on Elm Street can become a community garden or a parking lot. Please give your opinion and a reason.

turns.speaker: Ms. Ortiz
turns.text: I support the garden. Families could grow vegetables there, and neighbors would have a place to meet. Right now, our street has no shared space at all.

turns.speaker: Mr. Bell
turns.text: I support the parking lot. The shops on Elm Street lose customers because there is nowhere to park. Thirty new spaces would help the shops stay open.

turns.speaker: Mayor
turns.text: Thank you both. We will vote next week, after everyone has read the plans.

We will vote next week, after everyone has read the plans.

stimuli.title: Listen: Two answers

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: I got forty-five pencils. A box holds twelve pencils, and the teacher bought five boxes. Five times twelve is sixty pencils. Then the teacher gave away fifteen, so sixty minus fifteen is forty-five.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I disagree. I think the answer is seventy-five, because sixty plus fifteen is seventy-five.

turns.speaker: Leo
turns.text: But the teacher gave pencils away, so there are fewer pencils, not more. Also, I can check: forty-five plus fifteen is sixty, and sixty is how many we started with.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Oh, I see. Giving away means taking away. I should have subtracted.

items.stem: Why does Aiko want to use the pond scene?

options.text: It is more exciting than the storm scene.
It shows why Pablo made the boat.
She wants to write the caption tonight.
She likes to paint ponds.

distractors.a: This is Daniel's reason for the storm scene.
distractors.c: Aiko will write the caption later, but that is a plan, not her reason for choosing the pond scene.
distractors.d: Aiko never says anything about painting ponds. She says they can paint on Friday.

items.explanation: Aiko says the pond scene shows why Pablo made the boat, and she calls that the heart of the story.

support.clue: Listen for the word 'But' in Aiko's second turn. Her reason comes next.
support.frame: Aiko wants the pond scene because it ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'I want the zoo trip because we can see animals up close.' A choice is joined to a reason with the word because. Listen for Aiko's reason.

misconceptions.c: mixes up a plan with a reason
misconceptions.d: adds a detail that was not said

facts: Pablo and the Paper Boat is an invented story used only for this practice item.

items.stem: Sort each sentence: does it tell about Aiko or Daniel?
items.explanation: Daniel will draw the boat and liked the storm scene best. Aiko wanted the pond scene first and will write the caption.

support.clue: Listen for who says 'I want', 'I like', and 'I will'. Each speaker tells what they want or will do.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Lena will water the plants. Omar will sweep the floor.' Say the name, then the job. Sort the sentences by speaker in the same way.

facts: Pablo and the Paper Boat is an invented story used only for this practice item.

items.stem: Why did Pablo make the paper boat?

options.text: To get ready for the big storm
To win a boat race at the pond
To make a poster for the class
To send a message to his grandmother

distractors.a: The storm is a different scene in the book. It is not why Pablo made the boat.
distractors.c: The poster is the students' project, not something in Pablo's story.

items.explanation: Aiko says Pablo made the boat to send a message to his grandmother, who lives across the water.

support.clue: Listen to Aiko's second turn. She tells what Pablo wanted to do and why.
support.frame: Pablo made the boat because he wanted to ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Rita baked a cake because she wanted to thank her neighbor.' A character's reason is often a wish. Listen for Pablo's wish.

misconceptions.b: adds a detail that was not said
misconceptions.c: mixes up the story and the students' project

facts: Pablo and the Paper Boat is an invented story used only for this practice item.

items.stem: What decision is the town trying to make?

options.text: Whether to build a garden or a parking lot
Whether to close the shops on Elm Street
Whether to vote this week or next week
Whether to move the town meeting

distractors.b: Mr. Bell talks about helping the shops stay open. Nobody asks to close them.
distractors.c: The mayor says the vote will be next week. That date is not the decision.
distractors.d: Nobody talks about moving the meeting.

items.explanation: The mayor says the empty lot on Elm Street can become a community garden or a parking lot, and the town will vote.

support.clue: Listen to the mayor's first turn. The mayor names the two choices for the empty lot.
support.frame: The town must decide between ______ and ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'The class can choose a picnic or a movie day.' A decision names two options. Listen for the town's two options.

misconceptions.b: mixes up a reason with the decision
misconceptions.c: mixes up a plan with the decision
misconceptions.d: adds a detail that was not said

facts: The Elm Street meeting is an invented classroom scenario.

items.stem: Match each speaker to what the speaker says.

right.text: Wants a parking lot for the shops
Says the vote is next week
Wants a garden on the empty lot

items.explanation: Ms. Ortiz supports the garden, Mr. Bell supports a parking lot to help the shops, and the mayor says the vote is next week.

support.clue: Listen for each speaker's first sentence. Ms. Ortiz and Mr. Bell each start with 'I support'.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Dina wants a longer lunch because she likes to talk with friends. Paul wants a shorter lunch because he wants more time to read.' Match each person to the reason. Do the same with the town meeting.

items.stem: Which two reasons for the garden do you hear in the meeting?

options.text: Families could grow vegetables.
Children could play on the grass.
Neighbors would have a place to meet.
The garden would cost less than a parking lot.

distractors.b: Ms. Ortiz does not say this. Her reasons are vegetables and a place to meet.
distractors.d: Ms. Ortiz does not say this. Nobody talks about the cost.

items.explanation: Ms. Ortiz supports the garden because families could grow vegetables and neighbors would have a place to meet.

support.clue: Listen to Ms. Ortiz's turn. She gives two reasons. Mr. Bell gives different ones.
support.frame: One reason for the garden is that ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'One reason for a longer recess is that children need time to play.' A reason for an idea says what good it would do. Choose the two reasons Ms. Ortiz gives.

misconceptions.b: adds a reason that was not said
misconceptions.d: adds a reason that was not said

items.stem: Why does Leo say Priya's answer cannot be right?

options.text: Five times twelve is fifty-five.
The teacher bought five boxes of fifteen.
Giving pencils away means fewer pencils.
Sixty minus fifteen is seventy-five.

distractors.a: Five times twelve is sixty. Leo does not say fifty-five.
distractors.b: Each box holds twelve pencils. Fifteen is how many the teacher gave away.
distractors.d: Sixty minus fifteen is forty-five. Seventy-five is the answer to sixty plus fifteen.

items.explanation: Leo says the teacher gave pencils away, so there are fewer pencils, not more. Adding makes the number bigger, so Priya should have subtracted.

support.clue: Listen to Leo's second turn. He explains what giving something away does to a number.
support.frame: Leo says Priya is wrong because giving away means ______.
support.model: Mentor example. 'You can't have more cookies after you eat some, because eating means fewer cookies are left.' Words in a problem tell you which operation to use. Listen for Leo's reason.

items.stem: Who said each sentence? Sort Leo's and Priya's sentences.
items.explanation: Leo says a box holds twelve pencils and checks his answer with addition. Priya says she disagrees, and later says she sees her mistake.

support.clue: Listen for who speaks first and who answers. Listen for the words 'I disagree', 'I can check', and 'I see'.
support.model: Mentor example. 'Kim said the lake is deep. Ali said the lake is cold.' Name the speaker, then the idea. Sort each sentence by speaker in the same way.
